correctness.rationale: All six-vertex centrally symmetric polygons are three-segment zonotopes. The determinant-sum area follows from exact pairwise parallelogram dissection. In the basis of any selected generator pair, the unique minimum containing parallel-edge box has widths 1+|s| and 1+|t|, giving area S+(product of two excluded determinants)/selected determinant. Minimizing over three possibilities selects the largest determinant. The ordered-det inequality gamma S>=3 alpha beta is elementary and rigid. Equal determinants force an affine-regular hexagon. For sharpness, a standard-integral affine-regular model has area three and six chord directions; 715 all possible 3-/4-support-line systems are fully enumerated over exact fractions, each clipped to the containing square, and the minimum clipped area is four. Every chord enclosure can be tightened to a support system; its area is at least the clipped area. Code was run from the actual embedded content. The continuum proof is independent of the finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The exact three-determinant profile and classification of optimal edge-direction enclosures resolves the finite-direction version for all centrally symmetric hexagons and yields a sharp chord-bound with rigorous equality. Vigh 2026 defines chord quadrilaterals, proves sqrt(2) generally, proves the pentagon case and records the regular hexagon value, without this all-hexagon result. Classical Petty 1955 (as described by Fodor-Grundbacher 2025 and Vigh 2026) gives 4/3 for unconstrained directions, which does not logically imply the finite set of permitted chord directions; no exact edge-direction formula was found in the inspected text. The original Petty full text was not accessed, a genuine historical novelty risk.
residual_risks: The original Petty (1955) full text was not available for direct inspection; a previously known edge-restricted hexagon construction may exist in its proof or nearby classical literature.

value.rationale: The new 2026 chord conjecture makes side/diagonal restriction a natural structural question. A complete sharp inequality with equality rigidity for all centrally symmetric hexagons (equivalently, non-parallelogram one-fold planar translative tiles) settles an entire motivated shape class at a strictly stronger coefficient than the known universal chord sqrt(2) theorem. More significantly, the exact affine-invariant determinant area law computes a natural enclosure invariant over the full two-parameter family and classifies all optimal edge-direction pairs; it is not merely a regular-hexagon computation. No general Kuperberg conjecture solution is claimed.
